However, the specific mechanisms driving this dynamo action remain unclear. This study investigates the dynamo generation of magnetic fields in the convective envelopes of pre-main-sequence stars, focusing on the influence of rotation. We employed the anelastic approximation to model the convective envelope, incorporating a simplified equation of state and a simplified treatment of radiative losses. Our simulations utilized a three-dimensional, time-dependent, non-linear magnetohydrodynamic framework to examine the impact of rotation on the resulting magnetic fields. Our findings indicate that the rotation rate significantly influences the dynamo process. Specifically, rapid rotation leads to the formation of strong, large-scale, axisymmetric magnetic fields, whereas slower rotation results in weaker, small-scale, non-axisymmetric fields. Furthermore, we observed that the magnetic field strength is highly sensitive to the initial seed field.

In this work, we derive a new three-body Schrödinger equation that excludes two-body interactions and the two three-body bound states, known as Efimov states. This resulting equation is solved using the Faddeev approach, which yields a formula for the three-body scattering amplitude. This formula is expressed through Faddeev components of the three-body scattering state, which are determined by solving a set of coupled integral equations.
